title: Token-lock queue starvation — oncall diary and remediation sketch
content:
Summary:

This is a first-draft oncall diary and mitigation sketch from the token-lock queue-starvation incident observed early morning 2025-11-05 (PST). The incident manifested as a rapid rise in p95 generation latency, large numbers of OOMs on a subset of hosts, and large sustained queue lengths on the continuous-batching coordinator. Symptoms pointed to an emergent lock contention path inside the KV cache admission path that serialized batch progress and effectively starved worker queues.

Why this is different from previous KV OOMs: the memory pressure was not caused purely by unbounded prefetch growth or a single large runtime allocation. Instead we observed: (a) sustained micro-restarts of worker goroutines waiting on a token allocator lock, (b) coordinator micro-batches waiting while KV admission performed eviction/metrics updates synchronously, and (c) transient cache-miss storms which amplified eviction churn. Together these produced a token-lock cascade: token acquisition slowed, batch flushes held memory, eviction thrash ran, and hosts hit process OOMs.

Timeline (high level):
- 03:18 UTC: An uptick in p95 generation latency from 210ms -> 1.4s. Alert: SRE-BATCHING-LATENCY-CRIT.
- 03:20 UTC: First two worker processes OOM on host g-rw-uk-03; auto-restart by supervisor.
- 03:22 UTC: Queue depth (coordinator pending batches) rose from median 3 -> 18.
- 03:25 UTC: KV cache eviction rate spiked 8x; cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 66%.
- 03:27 UTC: Evidence in logs: repeated stacktraces where goroutines were blocked acquiring token_lock (stack snippet captured below).
- 03:31 UTC: Mitigation #1 (manual): throttled new traffic to model-id redwood/small-2x in region eu-west-1 for 8 minutes. Queue depth dropped gradually.
- 03:40 UTC: Mitigation #2 (hotfix): deploy config change to make KV admission evictions asynchronous (toggle admission.evict.sync=false) to reduce critical section duration.
- 03:45 UTC: Host OOMs subsided; p95 returned towards baseline over next 20 minutes.

Observed metrics and artifacts to review:
- Coordinator queue_depth.p95: spike from 3 -> 18 at 03:22 UTC.
- Token allocator lock hold time (sampled): median hold time increased 5x to ~12ms, p99 ~212ms.
- KV cache eviction/sec: baseline 15/s -> 120/s during spike.
- Memory RSS of worker processes: one host reached 86% of container memory just before OOM.
- Logs: repeated "waiting for token_lock" messages around 03:20-03:28.
- Heap profiles: ephemeral; we saved a heap profile from a restarted process at 03:28 (s3://redwood-ops/diagnostics/2025-11-05/token-lock-03-28.heap).

Excerpted log snippet (sanitized):

  goroutine 8425 [semacquire]:
  sync.runtime_SemacquireMutex
      /usr/local/go/src/runtime/sema.go:71 +0x47
  sync.(*Mutex).lockSlow
      /usr/local/go/src/sync/mutex.go:138 +0x105
  sync.(*Mutex).Lock
      /usr/local/go/src/sync/mutex.go:81 +0x3b
  github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/kvcache.(*Admission).AcquireTokens
      /workspace/runtime/kvcache/admission.go:214 +0x2a3
  github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/batching.(*Coordinator).reserveTokensForBatch
      /workspace/runtime/batching/coordinator.go:322 +0x1a1
  github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/batching.(*Coordinator).dispatchLoop
      /workspace/runtime/batching/coordinator.go:84 +0x4f

This indicates the critical path: admission.AcquireTokens holds token_lock while performing both admission bookkeeping and (sync) eviction decisions. When admission holds the lock for longer the coordinator cannot progress batches resulting in queue buildup.

Hypotheses (ordered by our confidence):
1) Admission critical section includes synchronous eviction and metrics updates. Under miss-storms eviction runs more frequently and takes longer (I/O/scan) which increases lock hold time.
2) Continuous batching depends on low-latency token acquisition; when tokens are not available the coordinator serializes more requests waiting on the same lock, causing head-of-line blocking.
3) Eviction thrash causes the cache to oscillate which increases cached object churn; churn increases memory pressure indirectly when batches hold items in-flight.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Traffic throttling on model-level route to reduce new inflight batches (applied via console / route override).
- Config toggle to make admission eviction asynchronous (reduce time in critical section).
- Increased cache admission concurrency knob on 2 hosts as an experiment (admission.max-concurrent=8 -> 16) to reduce per-op latency.
- Scoped host drain for two heavily impacted hosts while we validated fixes.

Short-term action items (next 48 hours):
- Code: Add instrumentation to admission.AcquireTokens to break down time spent: lock-waiting, eviction, metrics, bookkeeping. (owner: Priya).
- Infra: Add an alert that fires when token_lock hold time p95 > 50ms for > 2min (owner: Jordan).
- Product/Config: Roll out admission.evict.sync=false as a controlled experiment to 30% of traffic, monitor memory/regression (owner: Alexei).
- Runbook: Draft a short playbook entry describing token-lock cascade and the three-step mitigation (throttle -> async-evict -> host drain). (owner: Dina).

Longer-term engineering proposals (for RFC):
- Rework KV admission to hold lock only for token accounting; move eviction decisions to a lock-free or per-shard background worker. This reduces critical section duration and avoids head-of-line blocking.
- Implement per-model token buckets rather than a single global admission lock to reduce cross-model interference.
- Add hysteresis to eviction: avoid immediate eviction for transient miss bursts (small grace window).
- Improve batching coordinator backpressure: allow coordinator to route around waiting admission shards rather than stalling whole batch queue.

Runbook draft patch (quick):
- Detection: Alert SRE-BATCHING-LATENCY-CRIT + token_lock_hold_p95 > 50ms + coordinator_queue_depth.p95 > 10.
- Immediate response: 1) Apply route throttle for suspect model(s) to 40% of normal qps. 2) Toggle admission.evict.sync=false (via runtime config) if present. 3) Drain top 2 hosts with highest OOM count. 4) If OOMs continue, fail traffic to dedicated capacity for affected customers.
- Post-incident: Collect heap/pprof from restarted workers, capture token_lock trace, and create a follow-up JIRA RFC for admission rewrite.

Notes to self / open questions: 
- We still need to confirm if eviction work itself is CPU-bound (scanning large eviction candidates) or blocking on remote storage/metrics endpoints. Heap profile showed increased retention in transient batch buffers but not a single runaway allocation.
- Is admission already sharded per host? Need to verify exactly where token_lock lives in code and whether it is shared across hosts/containers.
- Can we add a temporary fast-path where admission.AcquireTokens returns a limited number of provisional tokens without eviction if queue_depth > threshold?

Debug commands and artifacts captured during oncall: (commands run are examples, sanitized)
- kubectl logs -n runtime coordinator-abc --since=1h | grep token_lock | tail -n 200 > /tmp/token-lock.log
- gdb attach <pid> && thread apply all bt > /tmp/backtrace.txt (used by SRE for postmortem)
- go tool pprof -http=:6060 s3://redwood-ops/diagnostics/2025-11-05/token-lock-03-28.heap

Follow-ups and owners: 
- Priya: Add fine-grained timing metrics inside AcquireTokens (timeline: 2 days).
- Alexei: Run canary of async eviction toggle to 30% and measure memory & latency delta (timeline: 24–48h).
- Dina: Draft runbook entry and attach playbook to Confluence (timeline: 48h).
- Jordan: Create JIRA-INV-4821 and RFC ticket for admission rewrite (timeline: create within 24h).

Retrospective notes (quick):
- Why did existing alerts not catch this earlier? token_lock hold time metric did not exist; we relied on p95 latency and OOM counts only. Add targeted metric.
- The human response path (throttle -> toggle -> drain) worked and prevented wider outage. However the hotfix (async eviction) is a risky change — need to verify it does not cause cache overgrowth in other workloads.

Appendix: short glossary and mental model for token-lock cascade: 
- token_lock: a mutex protecting the admission token pool used to limit aggregate in-flight tokens across batches.
- admission eviction: logic that runs when there are insufficient tokens and decides which entries to evict to free space. If eviction path runs synchronously under the lock it increases the critical section.
- miss-storm: rapid series of requests for non-cached keys that induces high eviction/miss rates.

End of diary. Add comments below for anything I missed — will fold into the post-incident timeline and the runbook PR.
